dial.summary: DXY edged higher to 100.42 and real yields held at 2.66% (near 18-year high) as the two structural macro headwinds persist, while M2 expanding to $103.6T, the Fed balance sheet flat at $6.75T, and near-zero BTC funding at 0.008% sustain three supportive forces; with TOTAL at $2.87T, BTC.D firming above 57%, and stablecoin dominance steady at 10.66%, the BTC Accumulation posture is maintained ahead of the data-dense September 30 triple-release (PCE, GDP, ADP) and October 2 NFP.

indicators.name: Global Liquidity (Global M2)
indicators.note: G4 M2 aggregate (Fed/ECB/BOJ/PBOC) confirmed at $103,616B (~$103.6T) as of September 18, 2026 per MacroMicro/StreetStats (6–8 week lag; July is the last fully reported month); US M2 alone reached $23.16T in June 2026 (+5.6% YoY, 28th consecutive monthly increase per GlobalMktObserv); 4-week trend up confirmed (expansion from ~$103.0T in late August to $103.6T in mid-September, +0.6% over 4 weeks); status supportive (4-week rising trend met); BOJ's September 18 hike (+25bps to 1.25%) will modestly affect yen-denominated G4 components going forward but has no near-term impact on the reported aggregate.

indicators.name: ISM Manufacturing PMI
indicators.note: August 2026 ISM Manufacturing PMI at 54.6%, down 1.0pp from July 55.6% (eighth consecutive month of expansion; released Sep 1, below 55.2% consensus); Production 58.3% (−0.2pp), New Orders 53.7% (−3.0pp), Backlogs 51.8% (−3.2pp), Employment 51.2% (−1.6pp); 4-week trend down (Jul 55.6% → Aug 54.6% = −1.0pp); September ISM releases October 1 — no new data as of September 22; status neutral (above 50 but falling; supportive requires above 50 AND rising; headwind requires below 48 and falling or above 62 — neither applies); S&P Global Flash PMI September 23 is the next advance read.

indicators.name: DXY (US Dollar Index)
indicators.note: ICE DXY at 100.42 on September 22, 2026 (up from 100.27 on September 21; dollar index edging higher after the previous week's +1.1% gain on hawkish Fed stance); 4-week trend up: ~99.0 (Aug 22) → 100.42 (Sep 22) = +1.42%, well above the 0.5% flat threshold; status headwind — DXY remains above the 100 threshold for the second consecutive session, confirming the structural dollar headwind; DXY above 100 joins real yields at 2.66% as the second active macro headwind; a sustained official close below 100 is required to return to neutral status.

indicators.name: Real Yields (US10Y - CPI)
indicators.note: FRED DFII10 (10-year TIPS constant maturity) last confirmed at 2.66% for September 18, 2026 (per StreetStats/TipsWatch); September 17 10-year TIPS reopening auction cleared at 2.653% — the highest real yield at auction since October 2008; Sep 19-22 DFII10 not yet published on FRED (H.15 lags by 1 business day); the 10Y nominal eased 4bps to 4.97% on September 21, but with breakeven at ~2.27% the TIPS yield remains near 2.65–2.66%; 4-week trend up: ~2.45% (Aug 20) → 2.66% (Sep 18) = +21bps; status headwind (rising 4-week trend AND above 2% absolute threshold both met); sustainably falling below 2% required to shift status to supportive.

indicators.name: 2s10s Yield Curve
indicators.note: September 21–22, 2026: 10Y eased 4bps to 4.97% on Monday (Sep 21); 2Y held at ~4.75% (last confirmed Sep 18, anchored to fed funds at 3.75%–4.00%); spread = 4.97% − 4.75% = +0.22% (+22bps); 4-week trend down (flattening): ~+38bps (Aug 21, pre-FOMC) → +22bps (Sep 22) = −16bps over 4 weeks, as the front end anchors to policy while the long end moves with economic data; status neutral (positive spread but not steepening; supportive requires BOTH positive AND steepening; deeply inverted < −50bps for headwind does not apply); curve narrowed 4bps today as nominal yields eased on softer risk tone while 2Y remains pinned; October 27–28 FOMC is the next key repricing catalyst.

indicators.name: Fed Balance Sheet
indicators.note: WALCL: $6,747B ($6.747T) for week ending September 16, 2026 per Federal Reserve H.4.1 released September 17 (Treasuries $4,554B, MBS $1,914B, other $279B); next H.4.1 release scheduled September 24, 2026 (2 days from now); 4-week trend flat: ~$6.70T (Aug 13) → $6.747T (Sep 16) = +$47B over 4 weeks, marginal expansion within the flat range; status supportive (holding at post-2022 stabilisation plateau; no change to QT pace announced at Sep 16 FOMC; marginal expansion driven by FX swap line activity, not new asset purchases); total assets up ~$138B year-on-year.

indicators.name: BTC Funding Rates (perps avg)
indicators.note: BTC perpetual funding rate at ~0.008% per 8h (CF Bitcoin Kraken Perpetual Funding Rate Index at 5.46% annualized as of September 18, 2026; spot-market range 0.0073%–0.0085% per 8h per MacroMicro/CryptoQuant); near-zero funding during BTC's move toward $84–86K on September 21–22 confirms the rally remains spot-driven, not leveraged; 30-day trend flat (funding has remained sub-0.01% throughout September as accumulation was orderly); status supportive (well below the 0.04% overheating threshold; near-zero is the ideal accumulation signal; Strategy/Saylor acquired 950 BTC for $75.7M in the Sep 14–20 week, adding institutional spot demand).

indicators.name: Stablecoin Dominance
indicators.note: Stablecoin market cap ~$307B (September 21–22, 2026; CoinGecko/CoinMarketCap); total crypto market cap $2.87T (TOTAL stable at cycle range); stablecoin dominance 10.66% ($307B / $2.87T); 30-day trend down: stablecoin dominance peaked at ~13% in Q1 2026 and has declined to 10.66% by late September as capital has deployed into risk assets; status supportive (30-day falling trend confirmed; headwind condition — rising dominance while TOTAL also rising — does NOT apply as dominance is declining); BTC dominance firming above 57% ($1.64–1.69T of $2.87T total); USDT ~60.57%, USDC ~24.1%; sustained sub-11% dominance alongside BTC.D firmly above 55% is the primary BTC Accumulation signal this cycle.

upcoming.title: S&P Global Flash PMI (September 2026, Preliminary)
upcoming.note: S&P Global US Flash PMI Composite, Manufacturing, and Services preliminary data for September 2026 at 9:45 AM ET — first advance September activity read capturing the full post-FOMC (+25bps Sep 16), BOE hold (Sep 17), and BOJ hike (+25bps Sep 18) tightening cluster; DXY at 100.42 and real yields at 2.66% (near 18-year high) are the two active macro headwinds entering this read; leads ISM Manufacturing (Oct 1) and ISM Services (Oct 5); a sub-50 manufacturing reading would materially shift November FOMC rate-path narrative; consensus expects modest softening from prior reads.

upcoming.title: Initial Jobless Claims (week ended September 19, 2026)
upcoming.note: DOL weekly initial jobless claims at 8:30 AM ET for week ending September 19, 2026 — labor market read in the first full week post-FOMC/BOE/BOJ tightening cluster; a sustained rise above 220K would signal early labor market cracks under fed funds rate of 3.75%–4.00%; prior weeks approximately 206K; labor resilience is key to the FOMC's case for sustained restrictive policy heading into October 27–28.

upcoming.title: Advance Durable Goods Orders (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Census Bureau Advance Durable Goods Orders for August 2026 at 8:30 AM ET — watch non-defense capital goods ex-aircraft (key business investment proxy for Q3 GDP); elevated borrowing costs (10Y ~4.97%, real yields 2.66%) and DXY at 100.42 weigh on capex decisions; ISM Manufacturing new orders fell to 53.7 in August (−3.0pp); Q2 2026 GDP third estimate follows September 30.

upcoming.title: University of Michigan Consumer Sentiment (September 2026, Final)
upcoming.note: University of Michigan Surveys of Consumers final September 2026 reading at 10:00 AM ET — first final sentiment read fully incorporating the post-FOMC (+25bps Sep 16), BOE hold (Sep 17), and BOJ hike (+25bps Sep 18) trifecta; year-ahead inflation expectations closely watched; a sharp drop in current conditions or spike in inflation expectations could shift November FOMC positioning; released same day as Advance Durable Goods.

upcoming.title: Conference Board Consumer Confidence (September 2026)
upcoming.note: Conference Board Consumer Confidence Index for September 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — forward-looking consumer sentiment after September's global central bank tightening cluster; a sharp decline from August would confirm elevated financing costs (real yields 2.66%, 10Y ~4.97%) are weighing on consumer psychology; August PCE was +3.7% YoY; August PCE print follows the next day on September 30.

upcoming.title: JOLTS Job Openings (August 2026)
upcoming.note: Bureau of Labor Statistics Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey for August 2026 at 10:00 AM ET — key Fed input for assessing labor market tightness; a significant decline toward 7M openings would signal elevated rates are cooling labor demand; October 27–28 FOMC will weigh this alongside September PCE (Sep 30) and September NFP (Oct 2).
